title: Front Wheel Bearing and Hub Removal and Installation
introduction:
The hub carries the wheel studs; the bearing lets that assembly rotate while supporting vehicle load. Think of a lazy Susan with a much tougher day job. Here, the front wheel bearing and hub come off together after the brake disc, grease cap and hub nut are removed.

I use the drawings to follow that stack from the outside inward, then rebuild it in reverse. This procedure applies to the listed 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications. Read it with the linked brake-disc, wheel and lifting instructions: those supply the access and completion work that makes this more than a hub swap on paper. It teaches removal and installation, rather than diagnosing whether a bearing caused a particular noise.

requirements.category: Prevent unexpected starting and protect yourself

items.name: Disable remote start and remove the key
items.detail:
Begin on a hard, level surface with the vehicle safely parked, the parking brake applied and the wheels chocked. Complete remote-start disabling first, if fitted, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. If the menu needs ignition ON, keep a valid key inside and the engine OFF: from ignition OFF, release the pedals and press the start button once; if already ON, leave it ON rather than pressing again.

For an automatic, establish engine-off ignition ON in the same way if it is not already ON, then hold the service brake and select Neutral in the ground-level cabin. With the parking brake and chocks maintaining restraint, release the brake pedal and press the button once to switch ignition OFF. For a manual, switch ignition OFF if it is ON, then select Neutral with the engine OFF while maintaining those restraints. Confirm ignition OFF and remove the key before hands-on service. Keep the parking brake applied throughout the job.

The ignition controls follow the Ford Mustang owner manual; service precautions are in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189). A remote or accidental engine start during service can cause serious personal injury or death.

items.name: Wear protective equipment
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp or pointed parts. Failure to use this protection can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Handle the cleaning materials safely
items.detail: Read the material safety information sheet before using the specified cleaner or lubricant; improper use can cause serious personal injury. Keep solvents away from ignition sources because they can ignite or explode.

items.name: Prepare the hoist
items.detail: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist rated for its weight, including cargo and modifications. Use the lift-arm locations in [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631). The drawing places the lifting points along the side sills behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels; identify each point by its stamped triangle. Lifting elsewhere can let the vehicle shift or fall, causing serious personal injury.

items.name: Keep the lifting equipment clear
items.detail: Position adapters and, on a two-column hoist, forks clear of suspension parts, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped. Avoid contact with the exhaust, steering linkage, axle and rear cover. Incorrect positioning can damage these parts. If using a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it.

items.name: Observe the lifting safeguards
items.detail: Do not power the drive wheels with the engine unless all drive wheels are off the ground; incorrect arm placement or grounded drive wheels can cause unintended movement, serious injury or death. If a jack is used during setup, use adequate capacity on a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block wheels remaining on the ground. Support the vehicle with floor stands before going underneath: a jack can lower unexpectedly and cause serious injury or death. The supplied emergency jack is only for changing a deflated tire; other use can damage the vehicle. Never jack against either bumper, which will damage its cover.

requirements.category: Have the parts and equipment ready

items.name: Replacement parts
items.detail: Have a new wheel hub nut and wheel hub grease cap ready. Have replacement caliper mounting bolts available for the fitted caliper; the brake-disc illustrations mark the removed mounting bolts for disposal, including the illustration for the two-piston arrangement.

items.name: Tools and materials
items.detail: Have torque equipment capable of the specified hub, caliper and wheel-nut settings, a suitable caliper support and a wire brush for the later mating-face preparation. Have Motorcraft® Brake Parts Cleaner - VOC Compliant / Motorcraft® Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A, PM-4-B, and Motorcraft® High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, ready. Control friction dust first; the wire brush is for the specified mating-face preparation, not for brushing loose brake dust.

items.name: Brake dust precaution
items.detail: Do not breathe friction dust or blow it from brake components with compressed air. Use approved dust-control techniques and avoid dispersing residue; it can present serious respiratory and other health hazards. Review [Brake and Clutch Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693183). Control dust before disturbing dusty components or beginning mounting-face preparation.

items.name: Home-garage preparation
items.detail: Do not judge asbestos content by appearance. EPA suggests professional servicing when the material is uncertain. If that is not possible and professional dust-control equipment is unavailable, its home-mechanic guidance describes wet wiping: use a low-pressure fine mist of water or detergent-amended water to wet the brake parts, then wipe them with a cloth. Keep bystanders, food and drinks away.

items.name: Contain dust and waste
items.detail: Do not blow dust with compressed air or clean it with a dry rag, brush or garden hose. Do not use an ordinary vacuum lacking HEPA filtration. Keep contaminated clothing and dust out of the house; change clothes and wash soiled clothing separately. EPA recommends double-bagging asbestos waste and following local disposal rules. Read the full [EPA brake-and-clutch guidance](https://www.epa.gov/asbestos/current-best-practices-preventing-asbestos-exposure-among-brake-and-clutch-repair-0) before starting.

items.name: Keep the instructions distinct
items.detail: This is EPA guidance for home mechanics, not a claim that every brake contains asbestos or that employer OSHA duties apply to your home garage.

items.name: Support the caliper
items.detail: Support the caliper and pads when positioning them aside. Never let the caliper hang from its brake hose; its weight can damage the hose.

items.name: Control friction dust
items.detail: Do not breathe brake dust or blow it from friction components or storage containers with compressed air. Remove it using government-approved techniques. Friction dust can present cancer and lung-disease hazards, irritate skin, eyes and the respiratory tract, cause allergic reactions and other chronic health effects, and result in serious personal injury. Seek medical advice if irritation persists. Review [Brake and Clutch Systems Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693183) before brake work.

items.name: Before removing the wheel
items.detail: If the wheel is cracked, deflate the tire before removing the wheel from the vehicle; failure to do so can cause serious personal injury. Never use heat to free a seized wheel nut because it can damage the wheel and bearing. A wheel needing welding or peening must be replaced; those repairs can lead to wheel failure and serious injury. See [Wheel and Tire Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693193).

items.name: Clean the mounting faces
items.detail: Before refitting the wheel, remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from its mounting face and the mating hub or brake-disc face. Ensure any rotor-to-hub fasteners are secured and do not interfere with those faces. Contamination or interference can let wheel nuts loosen and the wheel come off in motion, causing loss of control, serious injury or death.

items.name: Keep anti-seize in its intended location
items.detail: Apply only a thin coat at the interface between the wheel's central pilot bore and the hub pilot. Keep it off the wheel-to-disc mounting face, studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces; contamination can damage components. Wheel-nut torque applies to clean, dry stud and nut threads.

requirements.category: Lowering and returning to the parked state

items.name: Keep restraint continuous
items.detail: After the wheels are seated and their nuts initially finger tight, remove loose tools and clear everyone from underneath the car; keep the parking brake applied while lowering. Restore ground-wheel restraints as the tires meet the ground, then perform the final wheel-nut tightening specified above with the car resting on its tires.

items.name: Restore the grounded parked state
items.detail: After tightening, with the vehicle fully grounded, chocked and the parking brake still applied, restore its parked gear. For an automatic, enter the ground-level cabin with the valid key, release the pedals and press the button once from known ignition OFF for engine-off ON. Hold the service brake, select Park, then release the brake and press the button once for OFF. For a manual, keep the engine and ignition OFF and hold the clutch pedal down and select first gear. Confirm ignition OFF and remove the key before leaving.

edits.text: Remove the Front Bearing and Hub

NOTICE: Suspension fasteners are critical to the operation of vital components and systems. Their failure can lead to major service expense. If replacement is necessary, use the same or equivalent parts; never substitute a lower-quality part or a different design. Tighten every fastener to its specified setting.
edits.why: I treat the fasteners as working parts of the suspension. Correct replacement quality and tightening are part of the repair.

edits.text: Remove the brake disc. Refer to: [Brake Disc](#/document/G1693784) (206-03 Front Disc Brake, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: Start with the lifting preparation above, then remove the wheel nuts and lift the wheel off the studs as described in [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). Identify the fitted 2-piston, 4-piston or 6-piston caliper. Arrange the caliper support before undoing its fasteners. For that arrangement, remove the 2 caliper mounting bolts, located behind the caliper at its upper and lower attachments to the knuckle, and support the caliper and pads aside with the hose attached. The brake-disc drawings mark these bolts for disposal; the 4-piston and 6-piston text also explicitly requires it. Do not let the caliper hang from the hose. With the caliper clear, slide the disc outward over the wheel studs. This exposes the hub and its center cap.

edits.text: Remove the wheel hub grease cap from the center of the hub and discard it.
edits.why: The highlighted domed cap covers the hub nut. Removing it exposes the next attachment; this cap must be replaced during assembly.

edits.text: Remove the wheel hub nut exposed beneath the grease cap, and discard the nut.
edits.why: This is the central retaining nut highlighted in magenta. Once it is removed, the bearing and hub can come off the spindle. Keep a new nut ready for installation.

edits.text: Slide the front wheel bearing and wheel hub assembly outward off the spindle.
edits.why: The outward arrow applies to the highlighted assembly, including the flange and wheel studs. The bearing and hub are removed together in this procedure.

edits.text: Install the Front Bearing and Hub
Slide the front wheel bearing and wheel hub assembly inward onto the spindle.
edits.why: The installation arrow reverses the removal movement. With the assembly back on the spindle, the new central nut is the next part fitted.

edits.text: Install a new wheel hub nut and tighten it to 251 lb.ft (340 Nm).
edits.why: Use the specified torque to secure the bearing and hub assembly. The removed nut was marked for disposal, so it does not return to service.

edits.text: Fit a new wheel hub grease cap into the center opening of the hub.
edits.why: The cap closes the opening over the tightened hub nut. I check the drawing here to keep the order straight: hub, new nut, then new cap.

edits.text: Install the brake disc. Refer to: [Brake Disc](#/document/G1693784) (206-03 Front Disc Brake, Removal and Installation).
edits.why:
Use a wire brush and Motorcraft® Brake Parts Cleaner - VOC Compliant / Motorcraft® Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A, PM-4-B, to clean the brake-disc mating surfaces. Slide the disc over the studs against the hub, then return the supported caliper and pads to their mounting position. Install replacement mounting bolts in place of those discarded, and tighten the caliper bolts to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm) for the fitted 2-piston, 4-piston or 6-piston arrangement.

Complete the wheel mounting-face cleaning and pilot-only lubrication precautions above using Motorcraft® High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2. Position the wheel on the studs and install its nuts finger tight. Remove loose tools and clear everyone from underneath before lowering; keep the parking brake applied and restore wheel chocks as the tires meet the ground. With the vehicle resting on its tires, tighten the nuts in the star/cross pattern shown in [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Uneven tightening can produce high brake-disc runout and accelerate brake roughness, shudder and vibration. Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi); wheels can loosen after initial tightening, with a risk of serious injury.

With the car grounded and chocked, parking brake applied, and hands/tools clear of the fully assembled brakes, apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake-system operation. That check completes the linked brake-disc procedure; the hub nut disappearing beneath its cap is not the finish line. Restore the grounded parked gear using the completion preparation above, finish with ignition OFF and key outside, and do not drive if the brake-operation check is abnormal.

editorialRevision.scope: Known ignition states and continuous restraints, exact materials, EPA home-garage dust control, support-before-unbolting and grounded brake completion. Primary actions, branches and all values preserved.
